summary: A command exists only when Linear can serve it: no REST-path commands, no stubs that POST an empty document, and no command registered without a GraphQL spec entry behind it. Rate-limit budget is readable, and one noun emits one output envelope with the root --agent and --json flags never shadowed.
reason: Linear is GraphQL-only, so generated export, import, tail and integration write commands address paths that do not exist and always error, while advertising themselves in help and in the MCP tool list. A command that cannot succeed is worse than an absent one for an agent choosing from the surface. The envelope and flag-shadowing rules exist for the same reason: an agent that asked for machine output and got a human table has no way to tell.
validated_outcome: Root help and the MCP tool list carry no command that cannot reach a real Linear operation; 'rate-limit --agent' reports the live request and complexity budget with its reset instant; the four commands that used to declare their own --json honor the root flag.
